sources.provider: 日本地震工学会掲載資料（内藤多仲ほか1962年論文の図を含む復元版）
sources.observed: The foundation plan distinguishes an inner 80.00m dimension from an 88.00m dimension drawn through the foundation axes.
sources.adopted: 88m between model foundation centres. This is interpretation of a historical diagram, not an as-built site survey. Cap width/height and lower-frame interpolation are not measured from the scanned picture.

sources.provider: 日鉄エンジニアリング
sources.observed: Its Tokyo Skytree construction reference compares the Tokyo Tower base to a square with a side of approximately 88m.
sources.adopted: Independent engineering-company corroboration of the 88m nominal base dimension.

sources.provider: 東京都立中央図書館／国立国会図書館レファレンス協同データベース
sources.observed: Library research distinguishes the cited 80m width from the additional leg width.
sources.adopted: Do not equate 80m with the full outside tower footprint.

sources.observed: The official explanation describes deep foundation shafts and below-ground ties.
sources.adopted: No underground structure reconstructed from visible-cap dimensions.
Retain the relative south entrance rise supported by GSI samples and official parking access guidance. New apron edges are fitted to protected legacy city geometry, not a complete DEM.

inferences: Historical 88m axes mapped onto the current legacy local coordinate frame; geographic origin and individual surveyed foundation locations remain uncertain.
Lower-frame deformation is a bounded smooth interpolation, not a redrawing of measured steel members.
Foundation-cap dimensions and base-plate dimensions remain model estimates.
Apron side slopes are a local transition to existing city surfaces. They are not certified paths or a reproduction of the entire parking terrain.
At 14 facade-adjacent samples the legacy city under-building mask lies at -2m; the sample list and adopted adjacent-road 0.3m datum are recorded in the input file.
Historical GL and advertised observation-deck elevations use differing reference conventions; no global vertical correction is made in this increment.
